east_texas.headline: Sunny and warm today, with a cold front on Sunday.
east_texas.summary: Patchy fog in a few low spots early, and by mid-morning most backyard stations around Tyler read in the low to upper 60s. Sunny and warm this afternoon, with highs in the mid 70s, and Saturday looks about the same. A cold front Sunday brings a few showers and much cooler air for Thanksgiving week.

days.text: Mostly sunny and warm. A slight chance of showers after midnight.
Cold front. A 20% chance of showers, then turning cooler. West wind gusts near 25 mph.
A second front. NWS says rain chances are rising for late Tue into early Wed; timing still uncertain.
Cool and mostly sunny. Lows in the mid to upper 30s. Thanksgiving looks dry for now.

facts.p: Sunday's storms should stay below severe levels
No large outages in Smith or nearby counties

panels.title: Cooler, with a rain chance midweek
paras: NWS Shreveport expects temperatures near or a little below late-November normals after Sunday's front. A second front Tuesday into Wednesday may bring rain, and Thanksgiving Day looks dry for now.

The Climate Prediction Center gives better than even odds of below-normal temperatures for much of central and eastern Texas Nov 25–29. For Nov 27 – Dec 3 it leans cool and wetter than normal from the southern Plains to the Gulf Coast, with low confidence.

panels.title: A strong El Niño is in charge
paras: El Niño is now strong and still strengthening, near +2.5°C in the key Pacific region. That usually means an active southern storm track, with more rain and more cool, cloudy days in East Texas.
It does not bring Arctic air on its own. Ice or snow still needs cold air from Canada, and Canada is running warm right now.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NOAA Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, KLTV closings, PowerOutage.us, Weather Underground.

chips.text: Coldest night of the season Sat

nm.headline: Windy today, then a sharp cold front Saturday with brief light snow.
nm.summary: Sunny and windy today, with gusts of 30 to 40 mph in the high country. A strong Pacific front Saturday brings a quick round of snow showers, mostly under an inch, and drops temperatures 10 to 20 degrees. Saturday night is the coldest of the season so far, with single digits possible in high valleys. Sipapu opened for the season today.

days.text: Brief snow showers with the front, mainly morning to afternoon. Snow above about 6,000 ft; most accumulation in the northern and western high terrain.
Coldest night of the season so far. Teens and 20s in most areas, single digits possible in high valleys.
Sunny and chilly with light winds.
A quick system Monday night may bring a few snow showers. Little or no accumulation expected.
Another quick system may arrive Thursday into Friday. Significant snow looks unlikely.

nm.snow_note: Little change this week. The highest station is holding its snow; lower and sunny slopes are mostly bare.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu opened today with 1 of 6 lifts and 1 run. Its 12 in. base includes man-made snow. OpenSnow expects a few light refreshes over the next week and good snowmaking temperatures. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Strongest front of the season Saturday
paras: NWS Albuquerque says Saturday's Pacific front will drop temperatures 10 to 20 degrees. It is short on moisture, so snow will be brief. Flurries could reach as low as 5,500 ft, with any minor accumulation, under an inch, mostly in the northern and western high terrain.

Saturday night lows fall into the teens and 20s in most areas. NWS forecasts about 5 to 12 degrees at Angel Fire and near 10 at Red River. NWS suggests winterizing homes now; protect outdoor pipes and pets.

panels.title: Mountain roads in good shape this morning
paras: NMRoads lists no weather problems on NM-518, US-64, NM-434, NM-38, NM-75, NM-150 or NM-68. Yesterday's wet spots on US-64 in Taos Canyon and NM-38 have cleared. Expect road work on NM-434 south of Black Lake (MM 21–24).
Saturday's brief snow could leave slick spots on passes and in shaded canyons, and the cold Saturday night will refreeze anything wet.
NWS expects no critical fire weather for the next seven days. Fuels remain very wet.

panels.title: Strong El Niño favors a snowier season
paras: El Niño is strong and still strengthening. It usually sends more storms across the southern Rockies, which improves the odds for snowfall in the northern New Mexico mountains. It doesn't guarantee a big season, but the odds lean our way.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, Sipapu snow report, OnTheSnow projected openings, OpenSnow, Weather Underground.
